# ethereum-optimism/design-docs Weekly Report (Jun 14 - 20, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week focused on significant architectural refinement and repository maintenance, primarily centered on the `op-geth` decoupling effort and the evolution of ZK-related infrastructure. Developers advanced the design for L2 transaction representation, opting for class-partitioned accessors to better handle synthetic transaction types. The project also underwent a major cleanup, closing numerous stale issues and transitioning specific ZK development tasks to external repositories for better tracking. Technical progress was further marked by clarifications to the SDM protocol regarding block-level warming rebates.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Protocol & Execution Architecture
*   **SDM Protocol Refinement:** Defined precise intrinsic-warm exclusions for block-level warming rebates. This update clarifies which state accesses qualify for rebates, ensuring the policy is technically robust ([#387](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/pull/387)).
*   **`op-geth` Decoupling Strategy:** Significant progress was made on the design for migrating tests and creating `op-core/types`. A key decision was reached to partition L2 transaction accessors by class rather than using a generic wrapper. This allows the system to exclude synthetic OP types (like `0x7E` deposits and `0x7D` post-execution transactions) from standard Ethereum transaction lists while maintaining their functionality in specific contexts like Lagoon.

### ZK Infrastructure & Tooling
*   **CI/CD for ZK Proofs:** Discussions regarding ZK execution in development environments led to a consensus on using mock provers for CI and local work to manage costs. Proving on `op-sepolia` is being considered as a potential high-fidelity alternative if production infrastructure is established ([#21409](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/21409)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
*   **Stale Task Management:** A large volume of legacy issues related to task templates, test coverage, and justfile improvements were closed to streamline the backlog ([#351](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/351), [#360](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/360), [#699](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/699)).
*   **UX & Integration:** Long-standing discussions on Ledger detection and signing environment variables were closed, with the team favoring fresh design approaches for future signing UX ([#400](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/400), [#457](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/457)).
*   **External Resolutions:** Several issues were closed as they are now tracked in upstream projects or specialized Optimism repositories. This includes a critical `op-reth` SIGBUS crash fix (resolved in upstream Reth) and `ZKDisputeGame` bond credit claiming logic ([#19743](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/19743), [#21420](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/21420)).

### Active & Noteworthy Issues
*   **L2 Transaction Representation:** Ongoing work on [#20264](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/20264) and [#20265](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/20265) remains a priority. The team is navigating how to handle receipt index-correlation when accessors are partitioned and how to manage transition scaffolding that will eventually be deleted upon the final cutover to upstream `go-ethereum`.

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The week was characterized by high-level design coordination between maintainers regarding the Superchain's technical debt. The `op-geth` decoupling discussions show a strong emphasis on long-term maintainability, specifically avoiding the creation of new long-lived APIs for temporary transition scaffolding. Collaboration also extended to cross-project synchronization, as evidenced by the migration of ZK-specific monitoring tasks to dedicated repositories to better align with specialized development teams.
